name: Agent 37
oneLiner: Hosted Linux computers for agents, sold two ways: a prepaid Cloud API and a one-click personal-agent subscription.
whatItIs: Agent 37 is an early-stage company (Y Combinator, Fall 2026) running two products under one brand. Agent37 Cloud is a prepaid API for persistent sandboxes: a gVisor container by default, or a full VM as an option, whose whole disk survives between runs and which can sleep when idle.

Managed hosting is the consumer side: a flat monthly plan for a pre-installed OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Grok agent, with a browser dashboard, task board and chat channels. It has no public API of its own.
The split matters for this site. A non-technical buyer usually wants the second product, while almost every feature described here belongs to the first.
whoFor: Developers building one sandbox per end user, and non-technical buyers who want a personal agent without touching an API.
isolation: gVisor container by default: a user-space kernel, stronger than a plain container but weaker than a VM, and Docker does not work inside it. The vm type gives a full VM with its own kernel at 2.5× compute; performance gives dedicated cores at 4×.
sizes: Four shapes, with 4 vCPU as the ceiling on the default type: 2/4, 4/8, 4/16 and 4/32 vCPU/GB. Disk is any whole number of GB inside each shape's range, defaulting to 4, 6, 12 or 24 GB.

billing.model: Prepaid wallet, no subscription and no plan fee.
billing.meter: Per minute, priced from the shape you reserved: $0.80 per vCPU-month, $0.70 per GB-month, $0.09 per GB-month of disk.
billing.stopped: Disk only. A sleep checkpoint keeps memory at no extra charge; a stopped instance loses memory and still pays for disk.
billing.planFee: None on the Cloud API. The personal plans ($3.99 to $99.99 a month) are a separate product.
billing.minimum: No minimum charge, but creating an instance requires one day of its running cost in the wallet.

A.headline: ≈ $1.09 a month
A.shape: 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, 4 GB disk (the entry shape), deleted after each task
notes: The requested shape exists exactly, so no substitution is needed.
Boot and provisioning time is not billed; transitional states such as starting and stopping are billed at the full rate.
Excludes model tokens, which usually dominate the cost of a ten-minute agent task.

B.headline: ≈ $10.60 or $30.10 a month
B.shape: The requested 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 50 GB box does not exist as a single shape.

lines.label: 4 vCPU / 8 GB, 20 GB disk (the disk cap on this shape)
4 vCPU / 32 GB, 50 GB disk (the nearest shape that allows 50 GB)

notes: A VM, needed for Docker or /dev/kvm, multiplies compute by 2.5: about $23.85 or $68.59.
Both figures match the vendor's own shape table plus disk at $0.09/GB-month.
B.flag: 50 GB of disk forces the 4 vCPU / 32 GB shape. If 20 GB is enough, the same CPU and RAM cost a third as much.

C.headline: ≈ $1.61 or $2.86 a month
C.shape: The requested 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 20 GB box does not exist: that shape caps disk at 12 GB.
notes: A 30-day month is 720 hours, so disk is prorated over 720/730 of a month.
At 90 awake hours, disk is two-thirds of the bill in the first option.
Leaving the same box running all month instead would cost about $5.40.
C.flag: 20 GB is not orderable with 2 vCPU. The second line buys more CPU and RAM than asked to get the disk.

usability.dashboard: Yes, two of them: agent37.com/dashboard/cloud for keys, billing, team and metrics, and a separate dashboard for the personal-agent product. The docs never describe creating a Cloud sandbox by clicking, so the documented path is an API call or the CLI.
usability.withoutCode: On managed hosting, yes, that is the whole product: one click, a task board, a web terminal, a file browser and a live desktop. On the Cloud API, no: every create path in the docs is `POST /v1/instances`, `npx agent37`, or a code snippet.
usability.signup: Cloud needs a card to unlock the $5 starter credit, or you can sign up through the API with no credit and fund it first. The personal free plan needs no card.
usability.docs: Mintlify docs, over 60 pages, runnable examples for every endpoint, and `llms.txt` bundles so an agent can read the whole manual. Support is a founder's email, a dashboard chat bubble and a booking link. There is a public status page.
tripsUp: The vocabulary is developer-native: instance, template, exec, signed URL, default port.
The first step on the Cloud product is a terminal or an HTTP request.
Two dashboards and two products share one brand, and the pricing page covers only the Cloud one.
Sleep versus stop is a billing decision disguised as a lifecycle decision.
Stopped is not free: disk bills until you delete the instance.
Managed model calls fail by default because the per-instance budget starts at zero.

caveats.detail: The sizing page says 4 vCPU is the ceiling on every instance type and that a request for 16 vCPU comes back as 4. The VM page prices 8 vCPU / 16 GB and 16 vCPU / 32 GB. Both pages are current.

caveats.issue: battleships.dev models Agent 37 as having memory snapshots
caveats.detail: Its `snapshot: mem` and $0.03 figure describe the sleep checkpoint and cold storage, not a snapshot product you can name, list or clone. There is no snapshot product.
No per-GB rate, free allowance or overage policy appears on the pricing page or in the billing docs.

caveats.issue: Whether the Cloud dashboard can create a sandbox by clicking
caveats.detail: Every documented create path is an API call or CLI command. The absence may be a documentation gap rather than a product gap.

caveats.issue: Regions outside the US require the 2.5× VM type, and backups are stored in the US
caveats.detail: EU and India regions keep the instance and its disk local, but backups and the control-plane record are stored in the US.

caveats.issue: The $5 starter credit has moved before
caveats.detail: battleships.dev recorded a conflict between a $5 website claim and $1 in the billing docs. The billing docs said $5 on 2026-10-28, so it appears resolved, but the number has changed at least once.

strengths: The whole disk persists, not just a mounted folder.
Two pauses with different memory behaviour, both billed at disk only.
Free nightly backups of /home/node with seven restore points.
Managed hosting is the only genuinely one-click personal agent in this set.
Cheapest always-on 4 vCPU box of the seven at about $10.60 a month.
